messages:
Incident Bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert triggered: PROD model-catalog-service -> model-config-change (pager id PD-8821). Rule: config-validator > tokenizer-mismatch.

PagerDuty: Page fired to policy 'eng-oncall' (urgency: high). Escalation: Maya -> Devon -> Lucy.

Maya: ack'd. I'm on call. pulling logs now.

Devon: saw the PD alert, joining. any obvious customer impact?

Ajay: getting reports from support that some generate/embed calls returning 500 with "tokenizer mismatch" errors. Happening since the 01:12 UTC config rollout.

Maya: looking at model-catalog change events: automated rollout pushed change to default_model for "text-embed-v2" from "embed-v2@rev-24" to "embed-v2@rev-42" at 01:12:06. rev-42 was supposed to be a toy experiment and has a different tokenizer.

Devon: ugh. config validator should have blocked tokenizer changes unless flagged. Maybe validator missed because rollout used 'force: true' in the pipeline.

Lucy: echoing: customer-facing endpoints that use default_model (no explicit model pinned) will route to new revision. Likely cause.

Maya: mitigation plan: 1) route traffic away from catalog-default to pinned stable revision; 2) revert catalog default to rev-24; 3) disable auto-rollout pipeline until root cause verified.

Ajay: agree. I'll craft a quick routing override to send traffic for product tenants to embed-v2@rev-24.

Theo: tagging infra: we can inject a routing rule at the gateway layer to match on route "POST /v1/embeddings" and override model param. Less blast radius.

Devon: good. Maya, can you do a fast revert in catalog? I can deploy routing override.

Maya: doing revert now. Command: 
``` 
# revert default_model for text-embed-v2 in model-catalog
rbxctl catalog set-default --model text-embed-v2 --revision embed-v2@rev-24 --reason "rollback bad revision rev-42"
```

Maya: ran revert at 01:21:17 UTC. Catalog API returned 200. Pushed change id cc-20240318-77.

Devon: applying gateway override: 
``` 
# add temporary route override
kubectl -n prod exec gateway-0 -- /bin/sh -c "curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8080/overrides -d '{\"route\":\"/v1/embeddings\",\"model_override\":\"embed-v2@rev-24\",\"ttl\":300}'"
```

Devon: override applied at 01:22:05 UTC. Gateway reports override active.

Ajay: monitoring error rate on embedding endpoints.

Maya: checking logs: 01:12-01:21 window had ~12k embedding requests; ~2.6% returned tokenizer mismatch 500s. Affected customers: a small set of PLG accounts and one enterprise tenant (acme-corp).

Lucy: pinged Customer Success and sent a short note to acme-corp AM: "We saw transient errors on embeddings around 01:12 UTC due to a model config issue. We reverted the default and applied overrides; requests should be normal now. Follow-up and root cause forthcoming."

PagerDuty: Alert status: acknowledged by Maya at 01:18:02 UTC.

Maya: after revert+override, error rate dropped to baseline within 45s. No further 5xx spikes in last 10m.

Devon: suggest keeping override for 15m to ensure caches and in-flight routing settle. I'll set TTL=900 and monitor.

Ajay: digging into CI pipeline: the pipeline allowed a config with tokenizer: "tok-v3-experimental" to be promoted. The change author was an internal experiment branch; commit msg: "experiment tokenizer for embed-v2 rev-42". Need to add a validator to block tokenizer family changes without ML-approve.

Theo: can we add a quick guard in config-validator to compare tokenizer hash against approved list? Short term: block any change to "tokenizer" field in catalog unless PR has tag [ml-approve].

Maya: I will schedule a post-incident task to harden validator. For now, I'll escalate to oncall rotation: I'm handing off to Lucy in 25m.

Lucy: taking handoff at 01:40 UTC. I'll keep monitoring for 30m then open a follow-up ticket.

Devon: ops note: the rollback left one stale cached entry on edge nodes for 120s — explains the tailing errors. Confirmed stale caches cleared automatically.

Ajay: adding initial incident severity: sev-2. Customer impact limited to a few customers; transient, quick remediation.

Maya: creating incident record in incidents channel and starting a short RCA doc: 
``` 
+ Incident id: INC-20240318-embed-catalog-01
+ Start: 2024-03-18T01:12:06Z
+ Mitigations: catalog rollback @01:21:17Z, gateway override @01:22:05Z
+ Impact: ~2.6% 5xx on embedding requests for ~9 minutes. affected customers: acme-corp + small subset of PLG
+ Next: validator hardening, pipeline guard, postmortem writeup
```

Lucy: let me know if support needs templated text for customers. I can push out an update.

Maya: thanks all. I'm going to run a quick check on model catalog audit logs to see how rev-42 got promoted with force.

Devon: quick ask: can we add an automated check in router that rejects model revisions whose tokenizer differs from the currently active revision unless an explicit override param is provided?

Ajay: good idea. That would stop silent tokenizer drift.

Incident Bot: Incident INC-20240318-embed-catalog-01 created and linked to PD-8821.

PagerDuty: Incident status: resolved -> alert closed at 01:45:03 UTC by Maya.

Lucy: taking over watch. will post updates to incidents/INC-20240318-embed-catalog-01.

Maya: handoff complete. leaving notes in the RCA doc, will add timelines and logs.

Devon: I'll open a PR to add the quick gateway guard and disable the auto-promote flag for pipeline until ML signs off.

Ajay: will follow up with ML team to annotate approved tokenizer list and review experiment gating.

Lucy: thanks team. final ops summary to add to incident doc: root cause = bad default promotion of experimental revision with incompatible tokenizer; mitigations = revert + routing override; impact minimal but real; follow-ups = validator/gateway guard/pipeline change + customer comms.

Maya: closing thread, moving to postmortem drafting.

(automated system message): Thread archived after handoff and incident creation.
